title: Classification of Insurance Data
short: Insurance data classification using machine learning for risk assessment and data-driven decision-making.
body:
Efficient data management is essential for maintaining customer trust and ensuring regulatory compliance in the insurance industry. Insurance companies need accurate and efficient methods to assess and categorize risk based on customer and policy data. This process, known as insurance classification, plays an important role in risk assessment and fraud detection. By applying machine learning techniques, such as Random Forest classification, insurance data can be systematically analyzed to support more consistent, efficient, and data-driven decision-making.

Dataset

The dataset used for modeling consists of more than 50,000 real-world insurance claims recorded during 2025.

Model

A Random Forest model was used for classification and trained using an 80/20 train-test split. Hyperparameter tuning was performed to identify the optimal model configuration and improve predictive performance. Before training, the data underwent cleaning and imputation to address missing and inconsistent values. Categorical variables were encoded using target encoding, while one-hot encoding was applied to low-cardinality categorical features, such as age groups.

The resulting model achieved an accuracy of 93%. Feature selection and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis were also performed to identify the most influential features and better understand their impact on the model's predictions.

Interface

All project data, code, and related artifacts were maintained in a GitHub repository to support version control and future maintenance. In addition, an API was developed to provide the business team with access to the model and enable them to test its initial results. Postman was used to test the API and provide a practical way for new users to learn how to interact with and use the model.
